we have shown that the field of non-axial modes in a semiconductor laser can be approximated using a semiclassical approach, and that this approximation leads to good agreement with experiment.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of a magnetic field on the optical properties of a semiconductor.
the study of the dynamics of the optical field in a semiconductor laser.
the study of the properties of the radiation emitted from semiconductor lasers with inhomogeneous excitation, and in particular with the angular distribution of radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented here are in good agreement with the experimental data and that they are consistent with the theoretical predictions of the semiclassical theory.
the theory of the present paper provides a good explanation of the observed behavior of the laser modes in a wide range of the excitation conditions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonaxial modes of inhomogeneously pumped semiconductor lasers are characterized by a high degree of polarization and a narrow angular distribution of the emitted light.
the theory presented is in good agreement with experiment and that it is capable of describing the main features of the nonaxial modes of inhomogeneously pumped lasers.
we have developed a semiclassical theory for the field of a nonaxial mode and applied it to the problem of laser oscillation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular dependence of the emission intensity is determined by the spatial inhomogeneity of the excitation.
the lasing threshold of nonaxial oscillations in a laser with a rectangular cross section is higher than the threshold of axial oscillations by a factor of 1.5–3.0.
the angular distribution of radiation is determined by the shape of the inhomogeneous excitation profile, and that the angular distribution is independent of the gain profile.
